caption_used: Training loss curves over iterations for Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four SepLLM configurations. All models start with loss values exceeding 3.4 and converge as training progresses to 140,000 iterations. The Vanilla model achieves the lowest final loss at approximately 2.45, while StrmLLM (n=64) converges to roughly 2.60, showing a notable gap from the SepLLM variants. Among the SepLLM configurations, the H/T variant reaches the lowest loss at approximately 2.49, with SepLLM (n=128) settling at approximately 2.55, slightly above both the base SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) which converge near 2.51-2.52. The most rapid decrease in loss occurs within the first 20,000 iterations for all models, after which convergence slows considerably.
raw_response:
The plot displays training loss curves over iterations for five different model configurations: Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64, H), SepLLM (n=64, H/T), and SepLLM (n=128). The x-axis represents the number of iterations, ranging from 0 to 140,000, with tick marks at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents the loss value, ranging from 2.4 to 3.4, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The Vanilla model (purple line with no markers) starts at a loss value above 3.4 and rapidly decreases to a final loss of approximately 2.45. The StrmLLM (n=64) model (blue line with no markers) also starts above 3.4 and converges to a final loss of approximately 2.60. The SepLLM (n=64) model (orange line with no markers) begins at a loss value above 3.4 and converges to approximately 2.51. The SepLLM (n=64, H) model (green line with no markers) starts above 3.4 and converges to approximately 2.52. The SepLLM (n=64, H/T) model (red line with no markers) begins above 3.4 and converges to approximately 2.49. The SepLLM (n=128) model (dark blue line with no markers) starts above 3.4 and converges to approximately 2.55. All curves exhibit a steep initial decline in loss, followed by a gradual flattening as training progresses. The loss values for all models are consistently above 2.4 for the entire duration of training, with the Vanilla model achieving the lowest final loss, followed by the SepLLM (n=64, H/T) variant, then the SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) variants, and finally the SepLLM (n=128) variant, which has the highest final loss among the SepLLM variants. The StrmLLM (n=64) model consistently maintains a higher loss than all SepLLM variants throughout training.
